rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2<U+2013>3 report a two-year split-plot field experiment (2018<U+2013>2020) at Ludhiana with three N levels and seven drip irrigation regimes, measuring soil moisture, water balance, LAI, DMA, root mass density, N uptake, tuber yield and water productivity.
rows.notes: The study applies N in 16 weekly fertigation splits but never measures nitrogen leaching or volatilization, and has no non-fertigation or non-drip comparison. Its only related own results are deep drainage computed as zero in the water balance (Tables 5<U+2013>6; tensiometers at 60<U+2013>90 cm showing little fluctuation, Fig. 1) and N uptake by biomass and tubers (Tables 12<U+2013>13). The remark that rain may have leached applied N in 2019<U+2013>2020 is speculation citing other work, not a measurement. The study therefore shows at most a precondition (no drainage, high N uptake), not reduced N loss via split fertigation.

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2<U+2013>3, two-year field experiment on potato under surface and subsurface drip. Q2: Section 3.3 and Fig. 2a,b report that subsurface drip treatments had the highest root mass density in the 15<U+2013>30 cm layer (40<U+2013>43% of RMD) versus surface drip with 65% in 0<U+2013>15 cm; Section 3.5/Tables 12<U+2013>13 show higher N uptake in I1<U+2013>I3 than I7; Section 3.4/Table 10 shows highest tuber yield in I1<U+2013>I3, attributed by the authors to higher RMD at 15<U+2013>30 cm leading to more N uptake. Q4: intermediate variables measured <U+2014> soil moisture distribution by FDR and tensiometers (Tables 3<U+2013>4, Fig. 1), root mass density by core sampling (Fig. 2), N uptake (Tables 12<U+2013>13), and transpiration partitioned from ET (Table 7), with yield regressed on transpiration (Fig. 6, R2 0.92). Q9: standard errors given in parentheses for tuber yield (Table 10), tuber weight and number (Table 11), LAI (Table 8) and DMA (Table 9), plus LSD values.
rows.notes: Evidence concerns subsurface versus surface drip and irrigation level, not drip versus non-drip irrigation; the 'deeper root' effect is specifically for buried drip lines at 20 cm. Single site, single sandy loam soil, single cultivar (Kufri Pukhraj), plot scale. RMD figure reports only letter groupings, but yield and uptake tables give SE. No explicit limitations of the result are stated beyond noting year differences due to rain.

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2<U+2013>3 report the authors' own two-year field experiment on potato under drip irrigation.
rows.notes: The study contains no observations on weeds, weed germination, foliar disease or disease spread. The closest own result is that the 0<U+2013>10 cm soil layer stayed relatively dry under subsurface drip and wet under surface drip (Tables 3<U+2013>4, Section 3.1), which is only a precondition for the weed/disease suppression claimed in the passage. The passage's statements about planning, soil water-holding capacity and maintenance in sandy soils are also not findings of this study.

notes: Full text appears complete (abstract through references). Some tables and paragraphs are duplicated/garbled by PDF extraction but values are legible. The study compares subsurface drip regimes against surface drip at the recommended regime; there is no furrow or non-drip control, which limits what it can say about drip per se.
